The largest country in the world is Russia.

To understand the concept of relativity described in your text, imagine time as a river flowing at a steady pace for everyone. However, Einstein’s theory suggests that this river doesn’t flow at the same speed everywhere.

Think of it like this: Imagine you are walking through a crowded market (representing normal speed and gravity). You walk at your usual pace, and your watch ticks normally. Now, imagine you are on a super-fast escalator moving near the speed of light. To you, inside the escalator, everything feels normal—you can still read a book or sip your coffee without it feeling rushed. Your watch ticks at the usual rate.

However, if someone standing still on the ground watches you zoom by on that fast escalator, they see your movements in slow motion. To them, your watch appears to be ticking much slower than theirs. This is time dilation: time itself stretches out for the person moving very fast, relative to the person standing still.

Similarly, gravity acts like a heavy blanket draped over time. The stronger the gravity (like near a massive planet or black hole), the more the "blanket" weighs down on time, causing it to tick slower compared to areas with weaker gravity. So, time is not a rigid, universal clock; it is flexible and changes based on how fast you move and how strong the gravity is around you.
